name: Network Boundary Configuration Export
description: The effective ingress and egress rule set at the entity's external boundary, showing what can be reached from outside the system boundary and from where.

expected_content.element: Effective rule set with source, destination, port, and protocol for every boundary control point
expected_content.why: Effective rules, not intended rules; overlapping rule sets frequently permit more than any single rule suggests.

expected_content.element: Identification of every boundary control point in scope, including all accounts, regions, and virtual networks
expected_content.why: A single-account export from a multi-account environment understates exposure.

expected_content.element: Which rules permit ingress from any source
expected_content.why: This is the highest-signal element and should be readable without manual analysis.

expected_content.element: Documented intent for rules that are broad by design, such as a public web tier
expected_content.why: Broad-by-design and broad-by-accident are indistinguishable in an export without stated intent.

expected_content.element: Exposure status of administrative interfaces and management ports
expected_content.why: The most consequential and most common boundary finding.

expected_content.element: Reference to the reviewed baseline the current state is compared against
expected_content.why: Enables drift assessment, which is what converts this into period evidence when paired with EV-CONFIG-001.

source_system_examples: Cloud provider security group and network ACL export
Cloud security posture management exposure report

freshness_expectation.rationale: DriftGuard default for a continuously enforced configuration. Not an audit rule.

redaction_guidance: A boundary rule export is an attack map. Restrict distribution and never attach it to customer-facing output.
Internal address ranges may be tokenised provided rule structure remains assessable.
retention_guidance: Capture on a schedule and retain dated snapshots alongside EV-CONFIG-001.

validation_rules.rule: A boundary configuration export exists covering the in-scope environment.
All accounts, regions, and virtual networks within the boundary are represented.
Rules permitting unrestricted ingress to administrative or management ports are identified and carry documented intent.
For a Type 2 conclusion the export is paired with EV-CONFIG-001 evidencing that the rule set held through the period.
The export comes from the platform API or rule base rather than from a diagram or narrative.
The export is dated within the examination period or the freshness window.

common_issues.issue: Export covers the production account only, while non-production accounts share network paths into it.
common_issues.impact: Exposure through an adjacent account is invisible.

common_issues.issue: Broad rules present with no stated intent, so design cannot be distinguished from accident.
common_issues.impact: DriftGuard cannot conclude either way and must report insufficient evidence rather than a gap.

common_issues.issue: Single export offered as evidence for a full period.
common_issues.impact: Says nothing about rules opened and closed between snapshots.

source_refs.supports: Expected content, persuasiveness weighting, and the common issues list.
Freshness window, sensitivity classification, and redaction guidance.

notes: A broad ingress rule is not automatically a deficiency. A public-facing service is broad by design. Documented intent is what separates the two, which is why it is a required content element.
